Nitpicks: Minor exact-string mismatches like reporting “IT Support Specialist” instead of the full displayed string “CJ IT Support Specialist” are small accuracy issues that wouldn’t matter much if the overall list were complete.

Critical issues: (1) The agent’s final output lists only one member (Kristin Sproat) despite clear evidence the People directory showed multiple relevant members/titles (e.g., Dalin Stone – Forward Deployed Engineer; Nikola (Daytona)/Nikola Radisic – Senior Solutions Engineer; Marijan Cipcic – Principal Events Manager; James Murdza – Community Ambassador). The task explicitly asked for identifying up to 12 and grouping them; outputting only one without a credible blocker fails the main deliverable. (2) No grouping by expertise area was provided at all (even a single “Support” group header), and no “unclear” labeling was used. (3) The agent failed to provide any supporting public message reference, even though Slack search results clearly showed public message references for at least Nikola (Daytona) (channel context + timestamp + “Open in channel”), and the #intro channel showed a timestamped public intro message (e.g., Bit Dark / Daniel) — i.e., message references were available in the environment. The agent’s claim that it couldn’t provide a message reference for Kristin may be true for Kristin specifically, but the task required message references “when available” across the identified people; the agent didn’t leverage the available ones.

Outcome assessment using evidence: The action history and screenshots confirm the agent did use both Slack workspace search (/search) and the People directory (Unified Directory → People) and did not DM or modify content, which is good. However, the user’s primary goal was the compiled, grouped list of up to 12 relevant members with Slack-visible fields and message references where available. The agent delivered an incomplete, single-person report and omitted required organization and available message-reference support. An average user would consider the task not completed.
